english.title: Under 18 without reasonable excuse possess alcohol in a relevant place 3 or more occasions within 12 consecutive months
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person under the age of eighteen years, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AGE..), had in your possession alcohol, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ALCOHOL..), in a relevant place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PLACE..), on three or more different occasions, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INDIVIDUAL DATES..), which were within a period of twelve consecutive months
english.legislation: Contrary to section 30 of the Policing and Crime Act 2009.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person under the age of eighteen years
had in your possession alcohol in a relevant place
on three or more different occasions which were within a period of twelve consecutive months

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 30(2) of the Policing and Crime Act 2009 provides that a "Relevant place", in relation to a person, means:-
(a) any public place, other than excluded premises, or
(b) any place, other than a public place, to which the person has unlawfully gained access.
(ii) Section 30(4) of the Policing and Crime Act 2009 provides that for the purposes of section 30(2) a place is a public place if at the material time the public or any section of the public has access to it, on payment or otherwise, as of right or by virtue of express or implied permission.
(iii) Section 30(5) of the Policing and Crime Act 2009 provides that in section 30(2) "excluded premises" means
(a) premises which may by virtue of Part 3 or 5 of the Licensing Act 2003 (premises licence or permitted temporary activity) be used for the supply of alcohol, or
(b) premises which may by virtue of Part 4 of that Act (club premises certificate) be used for the supply of alcohol to members or guests,
